core.m1: A hotel is a place where travelers stay for one or more nights.
core.m2: You can book a room, check in, and ask staff for help.
core.e1: Our hotel is near the train station.
core.e2: I booked a hotel for two nights.
core.p1: I have a reservation at this _______.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="24" y="14" width="32" height="52" rx="6" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="58" r="3" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: A reservation is a booking made before you arrive.
core.m2: Hotels often ask for the name on your reservation.
core.e1: I have a reservation under Chen.
core.e2: Can you find my reservation, please?
core.p2: The _______ is under my family name.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="22" y="14" width="36" height="52" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M30 30h20M30 40h20M30 50h12" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m1: To check in means to register when you arrive at a hotel.
core.m2: You usually show ID and receive your room key.
core.e1: I would like to check in, please.
core.e2: What time can we check in?
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><circle cx="30" cy="36" r="12" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M42 36h22M56 36v8M62 36v6" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m1: A passport is an official ID for international travel.
core.m2: Hotels may ask to see your passport at check-in.
core.e2: Do you need my passport number?
core.p2: I left my _______ in my bag.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="22" y="14" width="36" height="52" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M30 30h20M30 40h20M30 50h12" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m1: A room key opens your hotel room door.
core.m2: Many hotels use key cards instead of metal keys.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><circle cx="30" cy="36" r="12" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M42 36h22M56 36v8M62 36v6" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m1: A single room is usually for one guest.
core.m2: It may have one single bed or one small bed.
core.e2: Do you have a single room available?
core.p1: I need a _______ for one night.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="16" y="36" width="48" height="20" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="20" y="28" width="16" height="8" rx="2" fill="none" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m1: A double room is usually for two guests.
core.m2: It may have one double bed or two beds, depending on the hotel.
core.e2: Is breakfast included with the double room?
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="16" y="36" width="48" height="20" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="20" y="28" width="16" height="8" rx="2" fill="none" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m1: A bed is where you sleep in a hotel room.
core.m2: You can ask about one bed or two beds.
core.e1: Does the room have two beds?
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="16" y="36" width="48" height="20" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="20" y="28" width="16" height="8" rx="2" fill="none" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m1: A bathroom is the place where you wash and use the toilet.
core.m2: Hotel rooms usually have a private bathroom.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="20" y="16" width="40" height="48" rx="3" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="52" cy="40" r="3" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m2: Hotels often give guests a Wi-Fi name and password.
core.e2: The Wi-Fi is not working in my room.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><path d="M18 50Q40 28 62 50" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M28 42Q40 32 52 42" fill="none" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="40" cy="54" r="5" fill="#8BA888"/></svg>

core.m2: Some hotels include breakfast in the room price.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><circle cx="40" cy="26" r="8" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M20 58c4-14 36-14 40 0" fill="none" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m1: An elevator moves people between floors.
core.m2: In some countries, people may also say lift.
core.e2: Take the elevator to the fourth floor.
core.p2: The _______ is next to the lobby.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="20" y="16" width="40" height="48" rx="3" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="52" cy="40" r="3" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: A towel is used to dry your body or hands.
core.m2: You can ask housekeeping for extra towels.
core.e1: Could I have an extra towel?
core.e2: There are no towels in my room.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><circle cx="40" cy="26" r="8" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M20 58c4-14 36-14 40 0" fill="none" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

core.m2: You can tell staff if it is not working.
core.e1: The air conditioning is not working.
core.e2: Could you check the air conditioning?
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="20" y="16" width="40" height="48" rx="3" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="52" cy="40" r="3" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: To check out means to leave the hotel and finish your stay.
core.m2: Hotels usually have a set check-out time.
core.e2: I would like to check out, please.
core.p2: What time do we need to _______?
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><circle cx="30" cy="36" r="12" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M42 36h22M56 36v8M62 36v6" stroke="#C8956C" stroke-width="2"/></svg>

phrases.en: I have a reservation under Wang.
phrases.zh: 我有一個用 Wang 這個姓氏預訂的房間。
phrases.note: Use this at the front desk when you already booked a room.

phrases.zh: 我現在可以辦理入住嗎？
phrases.note: Use this if you arrive before or near check-in time.
Ask this so you do not miss the hotel check-out time.

phrases.en: Could I have the Wi-Fi password?
phrases.zh: 可以給我 Wi-Fi 密碼嗎？
phrases.note: Use a polite question for hotel services.

phrases.en: Could you store my luggage after check-out?
phrases.zh: 退房後可以幫我寄放行李嗎？
phrases.note: Use this when your flight or train is later in the day.

dialogues.title: Checking In with a Reservation
dialogues.sit: You arrive at a hotel and already have a reservation.
lines: Hello. I have a reservation under Lin.
Welcome. May I see your passport, please?
Thank you. You booked a double room for two nights.
Here is your room key. Your room number is 405.
Thank you. What time is check-out?
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask if breakfast is included.
dialogues.tn: Focus on reservation, passport, room key, room number, and check-out time.

dialogues.title: Asking for a Room without a Reservation
dialogues.sit: You walk into a hotel and need a room for one night.
lines: Hi. Do you have any vacancies tonight?
Let me check. How many guests?
One guest. I need a single room.
We have one single room available.
How much is it for one night?
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask for a non-smoking room.
dialogues.tn: This dialogue helps students ask about availability, price, room type, and included services.

dialogues.title: Asking about Wi-Fi and Breakfast
dialogues.sit: You are at the front desk after checking in.
lines: Excuse me. Could I have the Wi-Fi password?
Of course. The password is printed on your room key envelope.
It starts at 7 a.m. in the lobby.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask where the breakfast room is.
dialogues.tn: Practice polite service questions with Could I / Is / What time / Where.

dialogues.title: Requesting Help with a Room Problem
dialogues.tz: 房間有問題時請求協助
dialogues.sit: You are in your hotel room and something is not right.
lines: Hi. I have a problem with my room.
I'm sorry to hear that. What is the problem?
The air conditioning is not working.
I can send someone to check it.
Thank you. Also, could I have an extra towel?
Of course. I will ask housekeeping to bring one.
dialogues.tp: Try again: say the shower has no hot water.
dialogues.tn: Students practice calm problem reporting and polite requests.

dialogues.title: Checking Out and Storing Luggage
dialogues.sit: It is your last day at the hotel, but your flight is in the evening.
lines: Good morning. I would like to check out.
Sure. What is your room number?
Thank you. Would you like a receipt?
Could you store my luggage until 5 p.m.?
Yes, we can keep it at the front desk.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask for late check-out instead.
dialogues.tn: Practice check-out, receipt, luggage storage, and polite follow-up questions.

speaking.q: What do you usually say first when you arrive at a hotel?
speaking.h: Start with: Hello. I have a reservation under...

speaking.q: What hotel service is most important for you: Wi-Fi, breakfast, or location?
You arrive early. Ask if you can check in now.
speaking.h: Use: Can I check in now? Is early check-in available?

speaking.q: Your room key does not work. Explain the problem politely.
speaking.h: Use: My room key does not work. Could you help me?

speaking.q: Role play: check in, ask about breakfast, then ask for the Wi-Fi password.
speaking.h: Try to use at least three phrases from this lesson.

culture.title: Hotel Check-In Etiquette
culture.photo: 📷 A hotel front desk with a guest showing ID and receiving a room key.
culture.notes: In many English-speaking travel situations, hotel staff expect a clear greeting, the name on the reservation, and one piece of ID. It is normal to ask about check-out time, breakfast, Wi-Fi, and luggage storage politely.
qs: What information do you need when checking in?
What question would you ask first?
How can you sound polite at the front desk?

culture.title: Asking Politely for Help
culture.tz: 禮貌地請旅館人員幫忙
culture.photo: 📷 A guest speaking calmly with hotel staff about a room issue.
culture.notes: If something is wrong in your room, explain the problem calmly and use polite requests such as Could you check it? or Could I have an extra towel? Clear and polite language helps staff solve the problem faster.
qs: What room problem might happen during a trip?
How would you ask for help?
What is better: direct complaint or polite request? Why?

words.tip: Put your tongue between your teeth, don't use /s/.
Voiced th — tongue between teeth, with your voice on.
Voiced th in the middle, not /d/.
Keep the th sound, don't skip it.

pronunciation.tip: This is a review of your very first pronunciation lesson. Mandarin doesn't have this sound, so it's easy to substitute /s/, /d/, or /f/ instead — slow down and check your tongue position between your teeth.
pronunciation.prac: My mother thinks these three clothes are the best.
